Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates bilateral hilar prominence and diffuse small nodular opacities, which corresponds to the classic radiographic presentation of sarcoidosis (bilateral symmetrical hilar lymphadenopathy with peribronchovascular nodules). This pattern helps distinguish it from lymphoma (typically asymmetric or massive unilateral adenopathy) and tuberculosis (often unilateral with cavitation or effusion).
